selected.lesson_subject: NP7 link-scan interval tuning and FGCP failover convergence
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: NP7 hardware link-scan interval controls cadence for link-state detection; distinct from generic FGCP heartbeat/election tuning
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: NP7 scans physical link state -> link-down indication reaches FortiOS/FGCP monitoring -> cluster failover and gratuitous ARP follow the detected event; interval bounds detection cadence, not election logic
selected.failure_class: slow link-down detection on NP7-based interfaces delays the start of failover convergence
selected.evidence_pattern: show full-configuration system npu; configured np-link-scan-interval; interface link-state transitions; HA event timestamps and GARP timing
selected.remediation_path: verify platform and NP7 support, tune only the documented scan interval within supported range, compare HA event and link-state timestamps, validate GARP and traffic recovery
selected.question_fingerprint: distinguish NP7 link-scan cadence from HA heartbeat, election and session synchronization
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: physical link -> NP7 link scanner -> FortiOS interface state -> FGCP monitor/failover -> GARP -> upstream switch
selected.semantic_review: PASS: no prior lesson teaches NP7 link-scan cadence; historical HA topics cover other triggers and election/session behavior.

selected.lesson_subject: FortiManager HA: manual versus VRRP failover, heartbeat timers and delta-sync queue
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiManager HA primary/secondary state replication using heartbeat and delta-sync queue; VRRP mode owns shared management address while manual mode requires operator promotion
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: primary records config changes -> delta sync queue transfers updates to secondary -> heartbeat/VRRP health controls role and shared address -> secondary takes over after failure; queue quota bounds pending delta state
selected.failure_class: secondary is stale or failover is delayed because heartbeat threshold, VRRP reachability, peer identity or delta-sync queue capacity is wrong
selected.evidence_pattern: HA status and peer state; heartbeat interval and failover threshold; VRRP interface/VIP; HA event log; file quota and delta-sync queue state
selected.remediation_path: validate peer serial/IP and cluster password, heartbeat path and VRRP interface, ensure shared management address routing, inspect queue/quota before forcing resync, test controlled failover
selected.question_fingerprint: choose correct HA mode and identify why VRRP or delta-sync evidence does not prove application-level recovery
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: primary FortiManager -> delta-sync queue -> secondary FortiManager; heartbeat/VRRP side channel -> shared management VIP

selected.lesson_subject: Asset Identity Center endpoint vulnerability enrichment through FortiClient EMS and OT inventory
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Asset Identity Center joins discovered asset identity with EMS endpoint vulnerability data and licensed OT/IoT vulnerability intelligence; distinct from log analytics and event anomaly detection
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: EMS connector supplies endpoint/telemetry context -> playbook Get Endpoints/Get Vulnerabilities actions retrieve records -> Asset List/Identity Center enriches asset with software and vulnerability attributes -> dashboards/reports expose risk
selected.failure_class: asset exists but vulnerability fields are absent or stale because connector, playbook action, license scope, endpoint identity or schedule is incomplete
selected.evidence_pattern: connector status; playbook execution result; endpoint and vulnerability action outputs; asset last-seen/source fields; subscription entitlement and dashboard filters
selected.remediation_path: validate EMS connector and permissions, confirm action inputs and scheduled execution, reconcile endpoint identifiers, check OT/IoT license scope and report time range
selected.question_fingerprint: distinguish asset discovery from vulnerability enrichment and determine which stage failed
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiClient EMS + FortiGate/OT sources -> FortiAnalyzer connectors/playbook -> Asset Identity Center -> vulnerability-enriched asset list/report

selected.lesson_subject: IEEE 1588 PTPv2 transparent and boundary clocks, E2E/P2P delay correction and Layer-3 transport
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSwitch PTPv2 transparent clock updates Sync correctionField for residence/link delay; boundary clock participates in BMCA and regenerates timing across VLANs; Layer-3 PTP added in 8.0
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Announce selects grandmaster -> Sync/Follow_Up carries time -> E2E Delay_Req/Resp or P2P PDelay exchange measures path -> transparent clock updates correctionField or boundary clock disciplines and redistributes time
selected.failure_class: wrong PTP profile/domain/transport/VLAN or unsupported clock mode yields offset drift, missing delay samples or no downstream synchronization
selected.evidence_pattern: PTP profile/mode/domain/transport; interface ptp-status/policy; diagnose switch ptp port get-link-delay; packet capture of Announce/Sync/PDelay and correctionField
selected.remediation_path: confirm model/firmware support, align domain/profile/transport, allow PTP VLAN on every participating port, account for IGMP snooping and avoid unsupported P2P combinations
selected.question_fingerprint: differentiate transparent versus boundary clock and E2E versus P2P delay evidence
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: grandmaster -> transparent switch with correctionField -> downstream slave; alternate boundary clock across VLANs with BMCA

selected.lesson_subject: WPA3 Beacon Protection: beacon integrity MIC, PMF dependency and Wi-Fi 6E/7 compatibility
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Beacon Protection adds integrity protection to beacon frames using a MIC in WPA3/PMF-capable wireless operation; distinct from rogue AP detection and client roaming
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: WPA3/PMF SSID advertises beacon-protection capability -> client and AP negotiate supported protection -> protected beacon carries integrity element -> client validates beacon integrity before accepting management information
selected.failure_class: feature is enabled on an unsupported AP/firmware or incompatible security profile, or clients cannot negotiate required PMF/beacon protection
selected.evidence_pattern: AP model and firmware; SSID security profile; pmf and beacon-protection settings; over-the-air beacon capture and client association result
selected.remediation_path: verify Wi-Fi 6E/7 model and minimum FortiAP release, enable PMF and beacon protection only on compatible WPA3 SSIDs, validate with capable clients and packet capture
selected.question_fingerprint: identify beacon-integrity protection versus rogue AP containment or protected data frames
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiAP WPA3 beacon -> MIC/integrity element -> client verification; separate association/PMF negotiation

selected.lesson_subject: FortiSwitch endpoint connection notifications: SNMP link traps, MAC notifications and FortiGate syslog
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC learns endpoint movement through alternative notification sources: SNMP link traps trigger L2 poll, FortiGate syslog MAC Add/Delete/Move, or FortiSwitch MAC notification traps; each has distinct latency and indirect-host coverage
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: endpoint connects/moves -> switch or FortiGate emits selected notification -> FortiNAC correlates switch/port/MAC -> L2 poll or direct MAC update refreshes host location -> access policy/enforcement engine evaluates new location
selected.failure_class: NAC does not update endpoint location because chosen notification source is absent, unsupported, delayed or unable to see hosts behind AP/indirect ports
selected.evidence_pattern: FortiNAC network-device integration mode; SNMP trap/syslog receive logs; MAC Add/Move/Delete event; L2 poll result; host switch/port/SSID attributes
selected.remediation_path: select supported notification method for the topology, configure traps/syslog on the correct FortiGate/FortiSwitch, verify source IP and SNMP credentials, run a controlled MAC move and compare host location
selected.question_fingerprint: distinguish link-up-triggered polling from direct MAC movement notifications and identify indirect-host blind spots
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: endpoint -> FortiSwitch/FortiAP -> FortiGate/FortiLink -> SNMP/syslog notification -> FortiNAC host-location update

selected.lesson_subject: RADIUS Change of Authorization and Disconnect with dynamic ACL attribute groups
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F Local RADIUS attribute groups construct RFC 5176 CoA-Request/Disconnect-Request and dynamic ACL payloads; distinct from initial Access-Accept VLAN assignment
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: endpoint session established -> NAC policy/state changes -> CoA or Disconnect request uses NAS/session identifiers and attribute group -> NAS returns ACK/NAK -> port/session policy is reauthorized or disconnected
selected.failure_class: NAS ignores or NAKs CoA because Calling-Station-Id/session identifiers, message type, attribute group scope or vendor DACL syntax is wrong
selected.evidence_pattern: Local RADIUS mode; attribute group and message type; Calling-Station-Id/Acct-Session-Id; NAS CoA/Disconnect logs; ACK/NAK and resulting ACL/session state
selected.remediation_path: confirm NAS support for RFC5176 and DACL format, map the correct device/logical-network attribute group, include required identifiers, validate CoA reachability and test ACK before policy rollout
selected.question_fingerprint: distinguish initial authentication VLAN attributes from post-auth CoA/Disconnect and diagnose a NAK
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F policy engine -> RADIUS CoA/Disconnect -> NAS session -> ACK/NAK -> dynamic ACL or session termination

selected.lesson_subject: FortiAuthenticator Cloud per-policy OCSP verification for EAP-TLS client certificates
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: RADIUS EAP-TLS policy performs online OCSP status check for presented client certificate with disable, enable and softfail behavior; distinct from SCEP enrollment and CRL download
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: supplicant presents client certificate during EAP-TLS -> FAC Cloud validates chain and policy -> OCSP responder queried -> good/revoked/unknown/timeout mapped to reject or softfail decision -> RADIUS result returned
selected.failure_class: valid user certificate is rejected or accepted unexpectedly because OCSP response, responder reachability, softfail mode or per-policy setting is misunderstood
selected.evidence_pattern: RADIUS authentication profile OCSP mode; OCSP request/response status; responder reachability and timeout; EAP-TLS result; certificate serial/issuer
selected.remediation_path: enable OCSP only on intended EAP-TLS policy, choose strict or softfail deliberately, validate responder DNS/TLS reachability and revoked/unknown/timeout cases
selected.question_fingerprint: distinguish OCSP good/revoked/unknown/timeout from CRL freshness and SCEP issuance
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: supplicant certificate -> FAC Cloud EAP-TLS policy -> OCSP responder -> status decision -> RADIUS accept/reject

selected.lesson_subject: SSH filter profiles: command interception, owner bypass and secret-scoped policy enforcement
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiPAM SSH filter profile evaluates commands within proxied SSH session and can exempt secret owner; distinct from SSH certificate authentication and session recording
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: user launches secret -> FortiPAM proxy establishes SSH session with target -> command stream inspected against assigned filter profile -> allowed/blocked/owner-bypass result -> session event/audit record
selected.failure_class: blocked command unexpectedly passes or valid command is denied because profile attachment, owner bypass, launcher path or proxy mode is wrong
selected.evidence_pattern: secret SSH filter profile association; owner identity/secret ownership; proxy launcher/session details; command audit and filter decision logs
selected.remediation_path: attach filter to intended secret or policy, review owner bypass semantics and command patterns, use proxied SSH launcher, test commands with owner and non-owner identities
selected.question_fingerprint: identify why command filtering differs for secret owner and delegated user without confusing it with certificate authentication
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: privileged user -> FortiPAM SSH proxy -> filter profile decision -> target SSH server; owner-bypass branch

selected.lesson_subject: Collector HA with VRRP VIP, leader/follower roles and process-health failover boundary
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Collector HA uses VRRP VIP for on-prem/AWS or load balancer for Azure/GCP; leader receives logs while Supervisor/App Server redistributes pull and performance jobs
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: devices send syslog to VIP -> VRRP leader owns VIP and receives logs -> Supervisor schedules pull/metrics jobs across collectors -> leader failure triggers follower VIP ownership and job redistribution
selected.failure_class: process-level collector failure does not trigger VRRP because network interface remains up; log transport and scheduled collection failover behave differently
selected.evidence_pattern: VRRP role/VIP owner; collector interface and priority; Supervisor job assignments; App Server 10-minute task-request timeout; log arrival at new leader
selected.remediation_path: separate interface/VRRP health from process health, use external load balancer health checks where needed, validate VIP L2 adjacency, test leader and follower failures independently
selected.question_fingerprint: distinguish VRRP interface failure from collector process failure and identify separate log versus polling-job recovery
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: syslog devices -> VRRP VIP -> leader/follower collectors; Supervisor/App Server job distribution side plane

selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiManager policy-package install synchronizes supported firewall/proxy policies, objects, SAML IdP settings, user groups and one-time schedules to FortiSASE under select-availability central management
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiManager objects created first -> policy package assembled and installed to FortiSASE target -> central management connector synchronizes supported objects/policies -> FortiSASE sync log reports success or per-object error

selected.question_fingerprint: distinguish FortiManager package installation from successful FortiSASE synchronization and locate object-level sync errors
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiManager ADOM objects/policy package -> central management connector -> FortiSASE policy objects/SAML/schedules -> sync log

selected.lesson_subject: Secure SD-WAN: minimum-sla-meet-members gating in Lowest Cost (SLA) rules
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: SD-WAN service rule uses minimum-sla-meet-members to gate rule eligibility based on the count of members meeting configured SLA; distinct from underlay bandwidth steering and BGP neighbor selection.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: health-check measures each member -> rule counts in-SLA members -> threshold comparison -> rule remains eligible or is skipped -> next matching rule selects fallback; zero threshold preserves legacy behavior when no member meets SLA.
selected.failure_class: alive members fall out of SLA and the rule unexpectedly remains eligible or falls through because threshold and fallback ordering are misconfigured
selected.evidence_pattern: diagnose sys sdwan health-check status; diagnose sys sdwan service4 <id>; per-member alive and SLA map; configured minimum-sla-meet-members; subsequent matching rule
selected.remediation_path: set a deliberate threshold, keep a later fallback rule, verify health-check targets/thresholds, test one-member and all-members-out-of-SLA cases
selected.question_fingerprint: distinguish link-alive from SLA-qualified and explain rule fall-through when minimum-sla-meet-members is not met
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: WAN members -> health-check SLA state -> member-count threshold gate -> primary lowest-cost rule or ordered fallback rule
